why: The relink queue lived only in handoff/PLAN-E2-C-relink-v3.md, in prose with checkboxes, and it was wrong twice: 3b was recorded as written into the tree when grep found zero hits, and item 8 said 'both places were fixed' when only one was. Both were caught by a human audit, and a human audit does not run itself on the day of the link. This file is the same queue as data, so tools/check_relink_queue.py can run it. P1 complete is the condition for linking; missing one item means a second relink.
expectationSemantics: `present` means the item is done and must stay done. `absent` means the item is NOT done and the tree must not quietly acquire it either -- an item that appears without its expectation being flipped is drift in the direction nobody audits. Flipping an expectation is a deliberate edit and shows up in the diff.

The figure is already reachable on the shipped artifact (engine prints it every stage, worker forwards it under `debug`, SDK already accepts `debug`), and emscripten_get_heap_size() is a constant 1073741824 because every profile links -sTOTAL_MEMORY=1GB without ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH -- so the field would have carried a number that cannot move, and d4-memory's slope criterion would have passed on it forever. items.title: the barrier's selection overshoots an EMPTY paragraph, so a successful mutation is refused -- OPEN, scoped 2026-08-16, not blocking
items.note:
This is finding 046's actual defect, now precise. Raw readback on the empty paragraph: `

E1-EMPTY-AFTER

` -- the bullet APPLIED and the read swallowed the paragraph below. Both browsers, both gestures. Not blocking this link: the fix needs a design (verify by block identity rather than refuse) plus its own measurement, and the link is for changes already decided. Round two needs a matrix cell for it. SCOPE MEASURED (findings/evidence/046/overshoot/, 8 cells x 2 browsers, frozen engine): EMPTY-PARAGRAPH-ONLY. The discriminator was a caret placed PAST the last character of a paragraph with text -- it reads one block and succeeds, so this is not the 'caret at a paragraph edge' failure finding 034 named. Containment holds on every overshooting cell, so a fix has to compare the read against the paragraph the action was dispatched on, not against the caret.

items.title: the input and clipboard traces are surfaced by the product -- DONE 2026-08-16
items.note: Firefox operator round: four IME commits advanced the revision once, and a real paste advanced it not at all. A control ruled out the shell -- four consecutive session.commitText() calls all advanced (0-1-2-3-4). So the loss sits between the browser's composition events and commitText, in HostInputAdapter -- and EditorSession accepts onInputTrace while web/e2-editor-app.js passes none, so that layer is the one layer nobody records. Next controlled variable: wire onInputTrace/onClipboardTrace into a page an operator can drive, and repeat the cell. RESOLVED IN PART 2026-08-16: the loss was found without the trace -- finding 050, the sink was never cleared, so every commit after the first was rejected as a buffer mismatch. Fixed and mutation-tested. What remains under this item is the trace itself: the product still wires no onInputTrace, so the next thing that goes wrong in that layer will be just as invisible. The clipboard half is now its own item. DONE: web/e2-editor-app.js now wires onInputTrace and onClipboardTrace, and toasts the FAILURES only (a toast per keystroke would be its own defect). Finding 050 was invisible for as long as it existed precisely because these went nowhere.

items.title: Ctrl+C now asks the engine for the selection -- DONE 2026-08-16, happy path unverified headlessly
items.note: The input adapter binds compositionstart/update/end, beforeinput and paste -- no `copy`. The clipboard adapter HAS copySelection(), and web/e2-editor-app.js never calls it (0 occurrences). The document is a canvas, so the browser's default copy has no DOM selection to take, and Ctrl+C leaves the clipboard holding whatever was there before. That explains the clipboard cell across four rounds: the only round whose paste moved the document was the one where the operator had copied something else earlier. NOT yet measured directly -- the reading is from the source and the round pattern, and it needs its own arm before it is called a finding. DONE: the product binds `copy` on its input sink and calls session.copySelection(), which asks the ENGINE for the selected text. VERIFIED: the handler fires and reports typed errors -- with no selection it now says CLIPBOARD_EMPTY_SELECTION where it used to say nothing at all. NOT VERIFIED headlessly: the clipboard write itself, because WebDriver blocks clipboard read/write (NotAllowedError). That half is what the operator round establishes, which is the same reason D5 exists.

items.title: finding 051: the 048 caret confirmation refused every click landing in the bottom half of its own line -- FIXED 2026-08-16
items.source: findings/evidence/051/, 2026-08-16; found while building the product-path harness
items.note: Not an engine change and not a relink: JS, in editor-shell/editor-session.js. `caretIsOnLine` compared |y - caret.y| against half the caret height, and caret.y is the TOP of the line box -- so the accepted band was half a line ABOVE the box plus the box's own top half. Measured on the shipped v2 artifact through the product page: a click at y=1739 with the engine reporting caret y=1418 height=414 (the box 1418..1832 contains it, and the engine's sourceSequence had advanced) failed twice at 30.1 s, while a click 200 twips higher on the SAME line confirmed in 0.3 s. The fix accepts the whole box with slack ABOVE it only. The stale-caret guard 048 exists for is unchanged and pinned by the same unit tests. Shell bundle v7 = e9668347…; v6 = 9b7e7d2a… stays as the record of what the four D5 operator cells ran on. E1-C divergence declared (third entry).

checks.text: the bottom half of a line is on that line (finding 051)

blocksRelinkSemantics: An item with blocksRelink true must be AS-DECLARED **and**, if it is declared absent, it is still outstanding work -- so P1 is not complete while it is open. Two items are deliberately false: the WASM heap field was withdrawn after measurement (2026-08-16), and the search-after-reopen wedge is an observation the product does not take today. Without this field the checker would report 'P1 complete' whenever every finished item was finished, which is the exact shape of a check that agrees with whatever it is shown.
externalAdjudication2026_08_16: fable, called as a subagent, refuted the premise that the two remaining blockers cannot be measured before the relink. Verified independently, all three claims: (1) tools/build_e2_discovery_profile.py COPIES the wasm (shutil.copy2, --wasm is an input), so a diagnostic profile can be packaged around the frozen 572035ac bytes -- no engine build, same engine; (2) the frozen wasm already serialises "readback":{"parsed": / "blockCount": / "itemCount": / "html":" and "containment":{"checked": (one occurrence each; "preBlocksObserved": zero, correct -- that is today's unlinked change); (3) all six worker patch anchors match exactly once in the FROZEN dist worker. Consequence: 3b's criterion and the containment ordering are both measurable now, for the price of a Python repackage plus browser rounds. Linking before that measurement would risk a v4, which costs the whole E2-B rerun plus E2-C D0-D5 again.

linkDecision.why: `p1Complete: True` means nothing is BLOCKING the link; it does not mean the link should happen now. Held deliberately so the newly characterised engine defect (queue-selecttext-overshoots-empty-paragraph) has a chance to ride along: it is an engine fix, so it can only ship through a link, and linking today would make it cost a second one.
